PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 1.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: EXT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL FOR BOYS - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: The forboding building looms on the horizon. Seconds later,
thick, leafy BRANCHES WHIP INTO FRAME obscuring our view.
At this very moment at the Longborough School
for Boys...
REVERSE ANGLE TO REVEAL YOUNG NED, in a WWII-era ARMY HELMET,
and EUGENE MULCHANDANI (wearing camouflage-colored orthodontic
headgear), hiding in the woods on a hilltop above the school.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...Young Ned had convinced Eugene Mulchandani
to go to war. For not only was it proof of
his undying patriotism...
With a salute, the boys run off into the woods.

scenes.heading: EXT. NORTH THRUSH WOODS - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Young Ned and Eugene fire stick guns at an imaginary enemy.
...it was also a much-needed hooky-playing
escape from an advanced geometry lesson in
proofs of the Pythagorean kind.
Moving through the woods, Eugene suddenly holds up a fist,
signaling Young Ned, who is coming up behind him, to stop.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
However, like all ill-advised troop
deployments, it did not come without its share
of unexpected casualties.
Pointing to his eyes, then to Young Ned’s eyes, before pointing
into the opening before him, Eugene silently signals for his
comrade to take a look-see. As Ned joins him, his jaw drops.
NED’S POV:
Ahead of them, a DEAD HUNTER is hung up in a barbed-wire fence.
BACK TO SCENE - MOMENTS LATER - FLASHBACK
Young Ned and Eugene stand aghast over the dead man, who has a
(tasteful) GUNSHOT WOUND IN HIS CHEST.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
Standing over his first combat fatality,
Eugene’s emotional radar was overcome, and the
onslaught of these emotional bogeys forced a
hasty retreat.
Eugene, full of terror and unable to take his eyes off the body,
slowly backs away... then turns and sprints. Ned watches him
go, but then turns back to the body.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Young Ned, on the other hand, stood his
ground. It had been...
Young Ned considers the dead hunter, an idea forming.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...4 months, 2 weeks, 3 hours and 31 minutes
since his father left him at the Longborough
School, never to return.
Young Ned slowly reaches out to touch the dead man... Then
pauses and reconsiders.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Which made this the precise moment he hatched
a plan to bring his father back into his life.
Plucking up his nerve, Ned touches the hunter and -- ZAP! -- the
hunter’s eyes open. Picking up the man’s shotgun, Ned questions
him.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Filled with heroic fervor, Young Ned
rationalized that if he could report who
murdered the hunter to the authorities...
Ned and the hunter converse MOS.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...the acclaim would not only garner him fame,
but also his father’s renewed attention.
Meanwhile, the hunter pantomimes his cause of death --
indicating he accidentally shot himself as he climbed the fence.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Alas, this hope began to fade when the hunter
revealed his cause of death was accidental and
self-inflicted. There was no murderer to be
caught...
Through the hole in the dead man’s chest, Ned spies a PARK
RANGER leading Eugene back to the crime scene. Ned quickly re-
deads the hunter.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED: (2)
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...though the park ranger would believe
otherwise.
The body’s THUD attracts the ranger’s attention. All the ranger
sees is Ned holding a gun and standing over a dead body.
Young Ned sits next to a sobbing Eugene.
Along with Eugene Mulchandani, both boys were
perceived by Papen County Juvenile Correction
Officers as anything but heroes.
Eugene’s blubbering only intensifies when the jail door CLANGS
open and his PARENTS first hug him, then shake an admonishing
finger in his face.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And while his comrade secured an honorable
discharge through the strength of his parental
allies...
Eugene’s parents escort him away and the cell door CLANGS shut
again. Young Ned approaches the door and cranes his neck to
look up and down the hallway, hoping to see his father.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...Young Ned realized that his father was not
going to fight his battles for him. For in
jail, as in life, he needed to take
responsibility for his actions.
OFF THE LOCKED CELL DOOR and sad Young Ned peering out.

scenes.heading: EXT. PIE HOLE - NIGHT (RE-USE FROM EPISODE 209, “LIGHTHOUSE”)

lines.text: CHUCK and NED burst onto the sidewalk as NED’S CAR pulls away.
It’s 20 years, 10 months, 8 days, 4 hours
and 17 minutes later, hereto known as “the
great escape.”
ANOTHER ANGLE as Chuck and Ned stare OFF CAMERA, the wind
carries LONG, UNSPOOLING MEDICAL BANDAGES INTO FRAME, that
eventually land at their feet.
This time it was not the Pie-Maker’s father
abandoning him; it was Chuck’s. Her long-
deceased but now alive-again father, Charles
Charles, had chosen to flee.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.
CONTINUED:
As a distraught Chuck bends down to gather up the bandages, Ned
fights off the panic growing in his gullet.
Dad!
That’s my car! He stole my car!
He’s gone.
What do you mean, “He’s gone”? A man wrapped
in bandages doesn’t just go. Not sans
bandages. He’s SANS bandages! That’s a no-go.
He’s not supposed to leave. I just got him back.
He’s not supposed to leave. He’s my dad...
This is really bad.
(losing it)
THIS. IS. REALLY. BAD... Really.
Ned and Chuck sit across from each other at the table. Ned
mumbles while resting his head on the table. Both are lost in
their own private nightmares.
Really... really... really... really... bad.
He just left. No goodbyes. No explanation.
No forwarding address.
At least my dad left a forwarding address --
to a new house, complete with a new family.
Now I know how you feel. Having him die was
horrible enough, but losing my dad because he
chose to leave is even more horrible.
(realizing)
I was dumped by my own dad.
You weren’t dad-dumped. I’m the one he was
mad at. He wanted you to choose. Me or him.
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED:
It’s my fault, dukes were put up and fistis
were cuffed. I’m the reason he left. And
after you risked everything to bring him back.
I risked you. I used you to bring him back
and it was selfish and wrong and now we’re in
this whole mess because of me... What if my
dad tells people about a pie-maker with a
knack for baking and waking the dead?
Career change. No more waking and/or baking.
I just want to hold your hand.
Chuck lays her hand on the table OUT OF FRAME.
Me, too.
Ned reaches OUT OF FRAME to take it. Beat... CAMERA PULLS BACK
TO REVEAL EMERSON sitting across from them -- HOLDING BOTH THEIR
HANDS, by-proxy, as he grows increasingly exasperated. After a
moment, he throws their hands down.
I’m done with this by-proxy hand jive. You’re
all acting lovey-dovey with each other when you
both oughta be squawking-mad. You screwed up
when you used his witchin’ finger to conjure up
a corpse and didn’t tell him about it. You
screwed up when you didn’t tap her pop when you
had the chance and I screwed up when I cahooted
and colluded to cover-up and dropped a certain
dead somebody else into ghost-dad’s empty grave.
But both you ladies should be squawking-mad as
hell at Dear Dead Dad for stealin’ your car and
stealin’ into the night with a corpse face
that’s not gonna be doing anybody any favors.
It is an unfortunate variable.
Hell, for all we know, his frightening
unvariables are flapping in the wind.
You know what? Now that you mention it, I am
mad. I’m furious. I’m--
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED: (2)
(cutting him off)
Get over it, fool. Bitchin’ and whinin’ time
just got the boot. We need to fix this.
At that moment, OLIVE wanders over to the booth.
“Fix” what, chitchatters? Wha’cha fixin’?
Fixin’ to tell you to mind your own.
Are you working a case?! Break it down. Are
there dead somebodies? Is it murder? Missing
persons? Who are the players? Lay it on me.
This is one of them need-to-know cases. And
you do not need, therefore you will not know.
Olive freezes in her tracks.
No casual case-chitchat to pass the time
whilst perusing the menu?
We don’t “chitchat” where we eat.
But I’m your Itty-Bitty. I’m helpful.
(hands her the menu)
Strawberry banana kiwi crumble. À la mode.
Golden cherry crimson pear. Also à la mode.
Just coffee for me, thanks.
Olive’s face falls as she takes their menus. She starts to turn
away, then stops. She clears her throat before turning back.
Hold up, yo. I am not a yo-yo you can jerk up
and down on a today-let’s-include-her,
tomorrow-let’s-not whim. ‘Cause if I am,
there are only so many knots I can tie in my
yo-yo string before it snaps for good.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED: (3)
Not now.
Please, Olive.
“Please, Olive” nothing. Where’s my pie?
Frustrated, Olive turns and struts away. Watching her go, Chuck
can’t help but feel terrible.
I hate this. Olive’s my friend. We can’t
make her our depository of secrets one minute,
and not good enough to participate the next.
(then)
Can’t we just tell her everything?
Hey, look at that, a dumb idea just found a
friend. Think again, we ain’t gonna poke a
stick up in our business and snap it off by
telling Little Big Mouth all our problems.
Little Big Mouth’s earned it. All she does is
trust and help us and all we do is lie to her.
We can’t afford to tell Olive. With all
that’s happened, we don’t need another
unfortunate variable.
Little did they know, another unfortunate
variable was already on its way...
Emerson sits at his desk, untangling a knotted skein of yarn.
...in the form of one-half of a renowned
synchronized swimming duo and sister
neurotics, who was called:
There’s a KNOCK on his door. VIVIAN enters.
Miss Vivian. To what do I owe the pleasure?
I need you to find someone for me.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED:
Opening her purse, Vivian pulls out a tastefully and lovingly-
rendered CHARCOAL SKETCH OF DWIGHT DIXON: He reclines on a
couch, shirt open. His ENGRAVED WATCH hangs from his neck,
suggesting the “Heart of the Ocean” sketch from Titanic.
VIVIAN (CONT’D)
Dwight Dixon. My gentleman caller. He hasn’t
come calling since our last rendezvous went
awry. Something horrible must’ve happened!
Emerson studies the sketch, covering his panic.
What makes you think that?
Because he cared about me. He wouldn’t just
leave without explanation. So he may very
well be lying in a ditch, with hemorrhagic
fever, as a pack of ravenous wolves circles
his broken body and the passing traffic drowns
out his desperate cries for help.
(then)
Even worse -- he could be dead.
(shutting this down)
Now, don’t go jumpin’ to conclusions. Let’s
start with the facts.
(then)
You say he was your “gentleman caller” -- how
many times he call on you?
Three.
He call you his girlfriend?
(shakes her head)
Give you a sock drawer?
(again, “No”)
Offer you bling?
No.
You have intimate relations?
(relieved)
Very. Long walks... clarinet concertos...
I meant, in the Biblical sense.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
CONTINUED: (2)
No.
Well, then, allow me to put this delicately:
men are dogs. They come around, barking up
your tree, but if they don’t see no kitty cat
in that tree, they’re gonna stop barking.
(off her horror)
Dwight ain’t missing. He’s barking up
somebody else’s tree.
Dwight wouldn’t do that. He’s a romantic. A
romantic who may need help.
I’m advising you not to look for Dwight Dixon.
Then find him for me so I don’t have to.
(sharply)
Listen. To. Me. You ain’t got any idea what
he was. He was a bad man. A sociopath. The
kind of man who’d stab a friend in the neck or
shoot ‘em in the back with a long-range high-
power sniper rifle. He’s gone away. Accept
it and stop tryin’ to get him back.
PUSH IN on Vivian as Emerson defames her beloved. She tries to
maintain her composure, but her heart is breaking.
Thank you for your time.
Vivian leaves. Emerson watches her go.
Emerson Cod hated dropping the bomb on Vivian
Charles’s heart. But a shock-and-awe campaign
was the only way to stop her search for
Dwight. For the facts -- as Emerson Cod knew
them and Vivian did not -- were these:
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. AUNTS’ HOUSE (RE-USE EP. 206, “OH OH OH... IT’S MAGIC”)

lines.text: Dwight dangles his watch in front of Vivian and Lily.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED:
Dwight Dixon was indeed a very bad man who
would do anything to get what he wanted. And
what he wanted was a watch.
Dwight lies next to Chuck’s open grave and opens the coffin.
He romanced Vivian and dug up her niece’s
grave, but found the watch missing and Chuck
still alive.

scenes.heading: EXT. CEMETERY - NIGHT (RE-USE FROM EPISODE 208, “COMFORT FOOD”)

lines.text: Dwight focuses his sniper scope on Ned and Chuck.
Intent on killing the people he believed stood
in the way of getting what he wanted, Dwight
failed to realize his murderous plan made him
the target...
Ned re-alives Charles Charles in his coffin. Dwight reacts. A
beat, and then Dwight keels over, dead.
...of a cosmic exchange that allowed Chuck to
keep her father alive, while taking Dwight’s
life in trade.
Emerson and Chuck pat the ground in front of Charles Charles’s
headstone with their shovels.
An accidental, inadvertent death that Emerson
Cod hid in order to protect his friends. And
so Dwight Dixon, villain and thief, was buried
in the grave once occupied by Charles Charles.

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - DAY

lines.text: Emerson pushes in through the front door. Ned and Chuck stand
behind the counter.
Cut me up a wedge of fresh and expensive and
make it on the house, ‘cause I just saved both
your asses a whole heap of grief.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED:
What happened?
Your Aunt Vivian paid me a visit. Tried to hire
me to find her missing paramour, Dwight Dixon.
What’d you tell her?
I said, “No need to pay me, I know where Dwight
is -- buried in the ground where I put him.”
What do you think I said? I said -- “No!”
Poor Vivian. She’s carrying a torch for a
flame I extinguished.
With my finger.
Don’t worry. I gave her plenty of reason to
forget about him. The last thing we need is
somebody investigating the disappearance of
Dwight Dixon.
Suddenly, the doors FLY OPEN REVEALING THREE STOIC NORWEGIAN
INVESTIGATORS. MAGNUS OLSDATTER steps forward as NILS NILSEN and
HEDDA LILLIHAMMER fan out behind him. Oddly, the Norwegians
mirror the Mod Squad in dress and physical appearance.
Goddag, friends. We’ve been consigned to
investigate the disappearance of Dwight Dixon.
OFF the Mod Squad’s concerned looks...
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 12.
FADE IN:
Magnus, Nils and Hedda step up to the counter and face-off with
Ned and Emerson. Chuck is conspicuously absent.
(already annoyed)
Hello... Magnus.
(feigning surprise)
Great Odin’s beard, if it isn’t Papen County’s
most surprisingly-successful private detective...
Picking up a slice of half-eaten pie off the counter, Nils
sticks it in his mouth and sneers as Hedda snickers and walks
OUT OF FRAME.
And his pie-baking, pretty-boy sidekick.
As flattering as that is, you’re still not
welcome here.
(turning; he snaps his
fingers and points)
You either, Hedda. Stay out of my kitchen.
As Hedda backs away from the kitchen doorway, CAMERA PULLS BACK...
INTO THE KITCHEN
REVEALING Chuck, in hiding. Suddenly, Olive slips in next to
her, looking around.
I’m still mad, so ignore my caring tone, but
why are we hiding?
Skubbe du...
“Skubbe” who?
Chuck was hiding to avoid a crack forensic
team from discovering she was infamous murder
victim, “Lonely Tourist” Charlotte Charles.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 13.
CLOSE ON A NORWEGIAN FLAG - FLASHBACK
CAMERA PULLS BACK TO REVEAL Magnus, Nils and Hedda, proudly
standing at attention in their official Norwegian police
uniforms and caps, in front of the enormous flag.
As proud members of the Norwegian Ministry of
Justice and Police...
CLOSE ON MAGNUS
Unctuous, as a FACELESS OFFICIAL pins a MEDAL to his lapel.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...lead detective, Magnus Olsdatter...
CLOSE ON NILS
Smirking as the faceless official pins a MEDAL to his lapel.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...his trusted criminalist, Nils Nilsen...
CLOSE ON HEDDA
Expressionless, as the same faceless official pins the MEDAL to
her lapel and winks at her.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and loyal profiler, Hedda Lillihammer...
CAMERA PANS a facility in which Magnus, Nils and Hedda are
busily working in their forensic coveralls.
...were an investigative trio without equal...
As each member of the team finishes their experiment, they give
the others a thumbs-up.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...until their beloved homeland, ranked an
astonishing 37th in the world in homicides...
The door to the lab opens REVEALING the faceless official and TWO
MOVERS with DOLLIES, who enter and remove their lab equipment.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...no longer deemed their services necessary.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 14.
The Norwegians stand in front of an enormous high-tech RV,
decked out with SATELLITE DISHES, ANTENNAS, GENERATORS, etc.,
with the words: “Mobile Investigative Lab Facility” painted on
its side. Staring OFF CAMERA, they cheer some yet-unseen reason
to celebrate.
They abandoned their motherland when reports of
a small place with a big murder rate, halfway
around the world, caught their eye.
THE NORWEGIANS’ POV:
CAMERA PUSHES IN ON A BILLBOARD for -- Norwegian Investigative
Services. Over an image of Magnus, Nils and Hedda are the
words: “SKUBBE DU? (Do you hustle?) WE DO.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Positive their forensic know-how and advanced
skill-set would make them a big fish in a
small-but-lucrative pond, they set up shop...
Suddenly, the billboard’s VERTICAL LOUVERS FLIP, REVEALING a new
façade that shows the smiling face of Emerson Cod and the words:
“In Cod We Trust! Papen County’s #1 Private Eye!”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...only to find themselves constantly and
consistently trumped by a large fish of
another kind by the name of Cod, Emerson Cod.
Magnus turns his attention to Emerson.
This new case is of particular interest to us.
You see, we’ve long attributed your domination
of the Papen County P.I. market to a secret
weapon of some sort.
Hedda joins him.
A psychic or savant housed in a shielded
section of your basement.
Regardless, we’ve enjoyed watching your career
skyrocket, but only because we’ll now take
even greater pleasure in watching you fall.
Nils joins Magnus and Hedda.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 15.
CONTINUED:
Today, our services were commissioned by
Vivian Charles to locate a man by the name of
Dwight Dixon. Imagine our surprise when
during our debriefing of our client, we began
to suspect you knew something about his
disappearance that you were not telling.
Tell us now and save yourself the humiliation.
I don’t know diddly or squat.
Unfortunately for you, the facts prove just the
opposite. Nils, refresh Mr. Cod’s memory...
Nils begins to recite the facts.
Fact one: Vivian Charles claims you refused
her case. History shows Emerson Cod never
turns down easy money.
History shows my docket was full. Just like
my pocketbook. It was nothing personal.
Fact two: When discussing Dwight Dixon with
Ms. Charles, you referred to him as a...
Hedda holds open an EVIDENCE NOTEBOOK and reads aloud:
...“bad man, a sociopath, the kind of man
who’d stab a friend or shoot him in the back.”
I was talkin’ her out of a bad relationship.
I didn’t know the man. It was conjecture.
Fact three: It wasn’t conjecture. You knew
from experience. You and Dwight hobnobbed in
the same circles.
The hell I did. We never nobbed hobs. And
definitely not in a circle.
Magnus holds up several CREDIT CARD STATEMENTS.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 16.
CONTINUED: (2)
We have copies of Dixon’s credit card
statements -- he was a frequent eater at this
very eatery.
(eyeing Emerson’s belly)
Which is clearly “home away from home” for you.
Therefore, establishing a reasonable link.
Not “reasonable.” Unreasonable. And purely
circumstantial. Also, a little rude.
Not for long. For I believe we will soon
prove beyond a shadow of a doubt that you’re
hiding something of importance to this case.
(skeptical)
Mmmm-hmmm... And how do you plan to do that?
With help from our Mother, of course.
We POP TO...
CLOSE ON a VANITY LICENSE PLATE that reads: “MOTHER.” CAMERA
PULLS BACK RAPIDLY TO REVEAL the mobile lab.
MAGNUS (V.O.)
The most sophisticated mobile investigative
laboratory facility of its kind...
CAMERA PUSHES RAPIDLY INTO THE SIDE OF THE VEHICLE--
CAMERA PULLS OUT TO REVEAL a state-of-the-art forensic lab.
MAGNUS (V.O.)
...providing instantaneous evidence
collection, inspection and documentection.
BACK TO SCENE
Magnus continues.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 17.
CONTINUED:
We both have secret weapons, Cod. If there’s a
shred of evidence connecting you to Dwight
Dixon’s disappearance, Mother will find it.
Ned’s heard enough.
Then you run home to your Mother because
you’re not welcome here.
(walking to the front door
and throwing it open)
This is my Pie Hole. No clues, no dirt, no
service. Now go.
If any diddly or squat should occur to you
that would be helpful in our case, you’ll find
us at the “Come and Sleep” motel. It was the
last place Dwight Dixon used his credit card.
(then)
Goddag, everyone. Hedda! Nils!
As he heads for the door, Hedda surreptitiously pockets
EMERSON’S FORK before falling in line behind her leader.
Blowing kisses, Nils brings up the rear.
Just remember -- Big Mother is watching. Any
last words?
Ned opens his mouth to respond, but before he can get a word
out, Nils has a COTTON SWAB under his tongue.
Awwwkk--!
As Nils corks the swab inside a test tube at his waist, Olive
suddenly appears and snatches it away. She grins, proud of
herself. Until Nils plucks a hair from her head with a tweezer.
Olive SCREAMS. Nils pockets it and marches out the door.
Wounded, Olive turns to the others.
What just happened?
NED / CHUCK / EMERSON
Nothing.
OFF of Olive’s glare--

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - KITCHEN - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: Somewhat stunned, Ned, Chuck and Emerson regroup.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
CONTINUED:
We got a crisis on our hands. We need to shut
those Norwegians down, pronto-mundo.
Also pronto-mundo, we need to find my dad.
Put Daddy Deadbucks on hold. We got to cut
these Norse fools off at the source.
But what if those Norse fools find Chuck’s
dad? Or worse, he finds them and tells them
what happened to Dwight. Not to mention the
waking and baking. If he wants me outta
Chuck’s life, that’s one way to do it.
All right. You go look for Daddy Deadbucks.
And someone needs to take another crack at
getting Vivian to call off the hounds while I
go see what these Norwegians dig up.
Collectively, they turn to look at Olive, who’s cleaning behind
the counter.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
(cajoling)
Oh, Itty-Bitty...
Me?! I’m “Itty-Bitty” again?! You mean it?!
As CAMERA PUSHES IN ON Olive’s excited-to-be-a-part-of-the-team-
again grin, we go--
Olive, her grin upside-down, sits on the sofa, talking to Chuck.
So “nothing” is something.
Yes, and you can help us turn that “something”
into nothing.
But you can’t tell me anything about the
something you want turned into nothing?
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 19.
CONTINUED:
All I can tell you is if you don’t convince
Vivian to call off her investigation of
Dwight’s disappearance, we could all be in a
lot of trouble.
What’d you do, kill Dwight?
(off Chuck’s shocked expression)
Just kidding...
(then)
You didn’t, did you?
Chuck twitters nervously.
Of course not, but--
Olive leans in, anticipating some dirt.
“But” what--?
But I still can’t tell you what happened.
Frustrated, Olive stands.
Well, hells bells, at least you could lie about
it. What hurts the most is the lack of effort.
None of you even try to hide the fact you don’t
want me in your super-secret powwows.
It’s not out of spite. We’re protecting you.

PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 39.
CONTINUED:
As evidenced by your dismissal of poor,
heartbroken Vivian Charles.
I was insensitive to the sensitivities of Miss

Would this be your confession?
Magnus takes a tape recorder from his belt, holds it to Emerson.

We don’t need your confession to solve this

Nils glances out the window to see:
THE NORWEGIANS’ POV:
Down below on the street, the Norwegians’ mobile lab speeds off.
BACK TO SCENE
Where’s Mother going?
Horrified, the Norwegians rush out of Emerson’s office to give

Looks like you been orphaned.
Stepping out onto the street, Chuck watches the mobile lab

Mother!
Ned at the wheel. Olive at his side.
Okay, first question: Do you know why Charles
Charles’s grave is empty?
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 40.
CONTINUED:
Yes.
You do, good... Was his grave robbed?
No.
No one took his body?
No.
Well, then what’d he do -- walk away?
Yes.
Chuck’s father is alive?!
Yes... Hold on--!
Wait, where are we stashing this hog?

Ned throws the wheel hard to the right. As Olive SCREAMS, the

The mobile lab heads across a grassy field.
OMIT
Ned white-knuckles the wheel as the vehicle accelerates.
Speed round: If Chuck faked her death and
her dad faked his death, was Dwight Dixon
on to them?
Yes.
PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 41.
CONTINUED:
And then he disappeared. Did you have
something to do with his disappearance?
Yes. I didn’t mean to. But I did.
(almost scared to ask)
And when you inadvertently, unintentionally
and without malice aforethought disappeared
Dwight...
(then)
...did you “disappear” him in a permanent

Um, I don’t understand the question.
(hesitant)
Did you kill him?
Dead end.
Is that an admission?
No! Dead end!
He points to the road ahead -- they’re at the cliff.
NED (CONT’D)
Jump--!
They SCREAM as a cliff’s edge rushes toward the windshield.
CAMERA PULLS UP AND AWAY REVEALING the mobile lab, with Olive

PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 42.
The Norwegians’ mobile lab speeds toward the cliff’s edge and

NED AND OLIVE
Clinging to a wispy branch on the side of the cliff. Olive

Thank God for my naturally-clingy nature.
They SLIP A LITTLE from the branch, with a SCREAM.
Olive, I’m sorry I got you into this. I’m

She looks up at him. He looks at her, hesitates, then:

Of all the secrets untold, this was the one

Olive blinks, stunned. She closes her eyes.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The Pie-Maker’s words unleashed a rapture in

Suddenly, a GLOVED HAND drops INTO FRAME.

PUSHING DAISIES #210 "The Norwegians" 10/08/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 43.

As the mystery man begins hauling Ned and Olive to safety...
Regrettably, who the Pie-Maker had seen would

Emerson pulls out a bottle of whiskey and pours himself a

Who Emerson Cod invited to his office was not.
For regretting his previous bad behavior, he
sought to make amends.
The door swings open, and Vivian enters. Her tone is guarded.

When the Norwegians exhumed the bodies of your

I’m not.

Knowing this will surely shatter Lily’s heart

It’s a good thing she has you to pick up the

As Vivian contemplated the emotional damage

(then, hurt)

Charles as my guardian angel.
